allowedSourceMaterial.overview: While investigating a young nun's rape, a corrupt New York City police detective, with a serious drug and gambling addiction, tries to change his ways and find forgiveness.

facts.overview: While investigating a young nun's rape, a corrupt New York City police detective, with a serious drug and gambling addiction, tries to change his ways and find forgiveness.
facts.title: Bad Lieutenant

visibleEditorialCopy.curiosityHook: Confronted by an atrocious crime, can a detective consumed by his own vices genuinely turn his life around before his spiral swallows him whole?
visibleEditorialCopy.description: In New York City, a corrupt police detective deep in severe drug and gambling addictions takes on the investigation of a young nun's rape, sparking an unexpected struggle to change his ways and find forgiveness.
visibleEditorialCopy.vibeSummary: Grim, emotionally heavy, and suspenseful; an uncompromising moral drama best taken with full attention alone.
visibleEditorialCopy.whyWatch: Abel Ferrara delivers a raw, uncompromising portrait of moral crisis, steering standard procedural grit toward intense personal reckoning and spiritual weight.

The remaining language ('atrocious crime', 'spiral swallows him whole', 'unexpected struggle', 'intense personal reckoning', 'spiritual weight') is figurative characterization, thematic shorthand, or metaphorical urgency. None of it functions as a meaningful new factual claim about plot mechanics, identities, relationships, motives, or causality under A_PRIME_PRODUCTION_MATERIALITY_V1. The copy stays at the premise and initial conflict, and it states no outcome for the detective's attempt at redemption and no later revelation or ending. No spoiler-boundary content appears.

sourceEvidence.notes: description: New York City, the corrupt police detective, the serious drug and gambling addiction, the investigation of a young nun's rape, and the attempt to change his ways and find forgiveness all restate the overview. curiosityHook: the atrocious crime, the detective's vices (drugs and gambling), and the attempt to turn his life around restate the overview. 'Atrocious' is evaluative characterization of a rape investigation. 'Genuinely turn his life around' paraphrases 'tries to change his ways'. 'Before his spiral swallows him whole' is metaphorical urgency. It implies a downfall is possible but names no event, outcome, or ending. The interrogative asserts no resolution.

whyWatch: 'moral drama' and 'procedural grit' are consistent with genres Crime/Drama and the police-investigation premise. 'Abel Ferrara' matches director. 'Moral crisis', 'personal reckoning' and 'spiritual weight' are thematic shorthand built on 'change his ways and find forgiveness'. 'Raw' and 'uncompromising' are tonal flourishes.

acceptedSemanticClassification: 'Grim' and 'emotionally heavy' match emotionalWeight=heavy and mood emotional. 'Suspenseful' matches moods. 'Full attention alone' matches attentionDemand=engaged and situations=[alone]. Keyword-only material (heroin, baseball, Catholicism, crucifixion, Christ figure, drug dealer, teenage girl) is not imported.

claudeAdvisory.uncertaintyNotes: The one near-threshold item is 'sparking an unexpected struggle' in description. The overview links the two only by simultaneity ('While investigating... tries to change his ways'), so 'sparking' turns that into a cause, and 'unexpected' is an unstated characterization. I read the phrase as narrative framing of the stated premise that names no event or outcome, so I kept it within tolerance. A stricter adjudicator could ask for 'sparking an unexpected struggle' to be softened toward the source's own 'while... tries to change his ways', in which case it would be a MINOR causal concretization. The curiosityHook's 'before his spiral swallows him whole' implies a downfall is possible, but it is posed as a question and names no outcome.
